title: Everyday Life
description: Ten short stories about everyday routines: mornings, getting to work and school, evenings at home and weekends.

lessons.title: Emma's Morning
lessons.summary: Emma gets up at 6, does the same three things at home and gets to work on time.
lessons.text:
Emma is 34 years old. She works in Boston. Every day, Emma gets up at 6. She always gets up at 6. She is never late for work.

Her work starts at 8. Before work, Emma does three things at home. First, she makes coffee. Then she gets her work things. Then she puts her work things in her bag.

Emma always keeps her bag in one place. She keeps it by the door. She never puts it in a new place. So she never has to look for it.

Emma does these three things every day. Before she goes, she looks at the time. It is 7:30. It is time to go! She takes her bag and leaves home.

Emma gets to work at 7:50. Her work starts at 8, so she is not late. Emma is never late.

Questions:
When does Emma get up?
Emma gets up at 6 every day.
When does her work start?
Her work starts at 8.
What does Emma do before work?
She makes coffee, and she puts her work things in her bag.
Where does Emma keep her bag?
She keeps her bag by the door.
Is Emma late for work?
No. Emma is never late for work.

lessons.title: Tom Runs to Work
lessons.summary: Tom gets up late, runs through the city to his company, and Ann helps him with his work.
lessons.text:
Tom is 25 years old. He works for a big company in Chicago. The company is in the city, and his home is a long way from the city.

Every day, Tom gets up at 7. His work starts at 9. But today, Tom gets up at 8:30! He does not have much time. It is too late to make coffee. Tom has to run.

Tom runs out of his home. He runs through the park. He runs through the city. It is a long way. Tom tries to get there by 9. He tries and tries, but it takes a long time.

At 9:10, Tom gets to the company. He is late. He is the last one to get to work.

Ann works with Tom at the company. She sees him and says, "Hi, Tom! Can I help you?" Tom says, "Yes! I have too much work."

Ann helps Tom with his work. With her help, Tom gets all his work done by 5.

Tom thinks, "Tomorrow, I want to get up at 7!"

Questions:
Where does Tom work?
Tom works for a big company in Chicago.
When does Tom get up today?
He gets up at 8:30.
How does Tom get to work?
He runs through the city.
Who is the last one to get to work?
Tom is the last one to get to work.
Who helps Tom?
Ann helps Tom with his work.

lessons.title: Lily's Second Day at School
lessons.summary: On her second day at a new school, Lily learns the names of the children in her group.
lessons.text:
Lily is 7 years old. She goes to a new school in Denver. This is her second day there.

There are 20 children in her class. The children work in groups. Lily is in a group with 3 other children: Max, Sara and Jake.

Lily does not know the names of the other children. So the teacher asks each child to tell the group his or her name. "My name is Max," says Max. "My name is Sara," says Sara. "My name is Jake," says Jake. "And my name is Lily," says Lily.

Then the group reads a book. Lily reads well, but there is one word she does not know. She asks Sara, "What does this word mean?" Sara tells her what it means.

It is only her second day, but Lily likes her new school.

At home, her mother asks her, "How is school?" Lily says, "It is good! Now I know the names of the children in my group."

Questions:
How old is Lily?
Lily is 7 years old.
Who is in her group?
Max, Sara and Jake are in her group.
What does each child tell the group?
Each child tells the group his or her name.
Why does Lily ask Sara about a word?
She asks Sara because she does not know what the word means.
Why does Lily like her new school?
She likes it because now she knows the names of the children in her group.

lessons.title: Sam's Team
lessons.summary: Sam's team meets in the morning, and Jo shows them a new system for the help service.
lessons.text:
Sam works for a company in Seattle. The company has a help service. When people need help, they call the service number. Sam and his team talk to the people who call.

Every day, the team meets at 9. Today, Jo has something new for the team. Jo is the head of the team. She shows the team a new system.

Jo opens the new system and shows the team how it works. She points to a number. "This is the number of calls today," she says. Then she points to a name. "And this is the name of the person who calls."

Sam likes the new system. With the new system, the team can see who calls and why. Now the team can help people better.

At 10, the help service opens. The first person calls the number. Sam talks to her. He opens the new system, and he helps her.

Questions:
Where does Sam work?
Sam works for a company in Seattle.
What do people do when they need help?
They call the service number.
When does the team meet?
The team meets every day at 9.
What does Jo show the team?
She shows the team a new system.
What does Jo point to?
She points to a number and to a name.
When does the help service open?
The help service opens at 10.

lessons.title: An Evening at Home
lessons.summary: Mark gets home from work, Ben finds Mia's little book under the bed, and Lisa reads it to both children.
lessons.text:
Mark and Lisa have 2 children, Ben and Mia. Ben is 8, and Mia is 5. Mia is the little one in the family.

At 5, Mark gets off work and goes home. Lisa works late, so Mark makes dinner for the family. While Mark makes dinner, Ben reads to Mia.

Both children love to read. Mia has her own little book, and Ben has his own too. Mia really loves her little book.

After dinner, Mia wants her little book, but she does not see it. Ben gets down and looks under things. Mia gets down and looks too. Ben looks under the bed. There it is! The book is under the bed. Mia says, "Thank you, Ben!"

At 8, Lisa gets off work and comes home. She puts the children to bed. While they are in bed, she reads the little book to both of them. Ben loves it too.

"I love you," Lisa says. "We love you too," say the children.

Questions:
Who are Ben and Mia?
They are the children of Mark and Lisa.
What do both children love?
Both children love to read.
Where is the little book?
It is under the bed.
What does Mia say to Ben?
She says, "Thank you, Ben!"
What does Lisa do at 8?
She gets off work, comes home and reads to both children.

lessons.title: Leo's Big Game
lessons.summary: Leo's school team never wins, but this Saturday they play really well and win the game.
lessons.text:
Leo is 12 years old. Every Saturday, he plays basketball with his school team.

The team plays every week, but they never win a game. Leo feels bad about it. The other children on the team feel bad too.

This Saturday, the team has a big game. Leo really wants to win. He says to his team, "We can win this game!"

The game starts at 10. Leo plays really well. He gets the ball, and he goes up high. The ball goes high into the air, and then it goes in!

The other team plays well too. But Leo and his team play even better. At the end, they win the game!

Leo feels great. All the children on the team feel great. Even the other team says, "Great game!"

Leo goes home and tells his family about the game. He really wants to play again next Saturday. He wants to win again!

Questions:
What does Leo play every Saturday?
He plays basketball with his school team.
Why does Leo feel bad?
He feels bad because his team never wins a game.
What does Leo want this Saturday?
He really wants to win the game.
Who wins the game?
Leo and his team win the game.
How does Leo feel after the game?
Leo feels great.

lessons.title: Kate Meets an Old Friend
lessons.summary: Kate meets her old school friend Rose at a little place in Austin, and they go around the city.
lessons.text:
Kate works in Austin. It is Saturday, and she has no work. Today, she meets her old friend Rose. Rose is in Austin for 2 days.

Kate and Rose are old friends. They are friends from school.

Where do the 2 friends meet? They meet at a little coffee place between Kate's home and her work. The place is next to a big school.

Kate gets there first. She looks around. Where is Rose? Then she sees Rose. Kate says, "Rose! It is so good to see you!"

Each friend has a coffee. They talk for a long time. Each friend tells the other about her work and her family.

Then they go out and look around the city. It is a big city, and they go around it for a long time. They find another little place, and they have another coffee there.

At 6, Rose has to go. Kate asks, "When can we meet again?" Rose says, "Next time, you come and see me in Boston!"

Questions:
Who is Rose?
Rose is Kate's old friend from school.
Where do the 2 friends meet?
They meet at a little place between Kate's home and her work.
Where is the little place?
It is next to a big school.
What do the friends do after that?
They look around the city.
Where does Rose want to meet next time?
She wants to meet in Boston.

lessons.title: A New House
lessons.summary: Ana and Paul have a new baby and move from the city to a big house, and their life changes.
lessons.text:
Ana and Paul live in Miami. They live in a little home in the city. Now they have a new baby. Since their home is too little, they need a big house.

Ana and Paul look at many houses. Then they find a house they really like. It is not in the city. The house is big, and it has a park next to it.

Ana and Paul have a new home, but they do not change their work. Ana works for the same company. Paul works at the same school. Since the house is not far from the city, they go to the city for work every day.

Life in the new house is new to them. Ana thinks, "Life here may not be the same. But it may be good."

Most of the people around them are good people. Many of them have children too. Ana and Paul make new friends.

Their life changes. Little by little, the new house becomes their home. They like most things about their new life.

Questions:
Where do Ana and Paul live?
They live in Miami.
Why do they need a big house?
They need a big house because they have a new baby.
Do Ana and Paul change their work?
No. Ana works for the same company, and Paul works at the same school.
What does the new house become?
The new house becomes their home.

lessons.title: Grace's Long Week
lessons.summary: After a long week at work, Grace comes home late, and her son Jack sets the table and makes dinner.
lessons.text:
Grace is a woman with one child, Jack. Jack is 15. During the week, she works long days. She is at work during the day, and she gets home late.

At the end of the week, Grace comes home at 8. Jack says, "Hi! Please come in. You should not do any work now."

Jack sets the table. He sets it for 2, for Grace and for him. Then he puts dinner on it.

Grace says, "Jack, that's great! Thank you." Jack says, "You work all week. You must be tired." Grace says, "I am. And I didn't have time for lunch."

"You didn't have lunch?" Jack asks. "Then you must eat a lot now."

Jack can't make a lot of things, but he can make this. Grace says, "I can't do all this without you, Jack. That's a great dinner." Jack says, "Please, have some more."

Jack thinks, "She works so much. She is a great woman."

Questions:
When does Grace work?
She works during the week.
What does Jack do?
He sets the table, and he puts dinner on it.
Why must Grace be tired?
She must be tired because she works all week.
Did Grace have time for lunch?
No, she didn't have time for lunch.
What does Jack say when Grace comes home?
He says, "You should not do any work now."

lessons.title: A Saturday Without Work
lessons.summary: At the end of the week, Mike has a slow day without work and reads in the park.
lessons.text:
It is the end of the week. It is Saturday, and Mike has a day without work. A day without work is very good.

Mike gets up very late. At 10, he is still in bed. He does not have to go to work, so he can do something new.

He takes a book and goes to the park. It is a big book about the world. Mike wants to see the world, and the book shows a lot of places.

There are a lot of people in the park. Some play games, and some talk. Mike reads his book.

At 6, Mike is still in the park. It is the end of the day, and the park is very good at this time. For Mike, this is the best part of the day.

Mike thinks, "This is such a good day! I have such a good time here."

At the end of the day, Mike goes home. He thinks, "Every week should end like this."

Questions:
What day is it?
It is Saturday, the end of the week.
When does Mike get up?
He gets up very late.
What does Mike want to do?
He wants to do something new.
What is the book about?
It is about the world.
Where is Mike at 6?
He is still in the park.
What is the best part of the day for Mike?
The end of the day is the best part.
